evidence_concerns.message: gnomAD presence is only partly fixed. Diagnostics keep their full gnomAD frequency and most are absent from gnomAD (148 of the 200, 386 of the 500), while background variants rarely are. The study's split check flags the gain of Rule + AVI over the rule-based ranking on the 200 SNV cases as possibly due to gnomAD presence in the all1kg check (results/snv_all1kg.json). In the main analysis the same gain is 0.0608 (0.0195 to 0.1149) in cases whose diagnostic is absent from gnomAD and 0.0 in cases where it is found; the difference, 0.0608 (-0.0063 to 0.1377), is not flagged. The split check tests two gains per SNV analysis, both from adding AVI (to the rule-based ranking and to the combined lookups), and none on the indel cases. The other tested gain is not flagged on the 200 or the 500. No other score was tested, so for GPN-MSA, GPN-Star, Evo 2, the single lookups and the combined models the limit is untested, not cleared. It is recorded in each protocol's limitations.

limitations: gnomAD presence is only partly fixed (README.md, Limits): diagnostics keep their full gnomAD frequency by design and most are absent from gnomAD, while background variants rarely are, so a score that learned gnomAD presence could pick the diagnostic for that reason.
Simulated cases: a ClinVar pathogenic variant is inserted into the rare variants of a 1000 Genomes person in the panel's genes. Lists are short and the people are not patients.
